we evaluated risk factors for uncommon histological subtypes of breast tumors using a centralized pathology review, which is more accurate than the local pathologist assigned ICD-O codes.

(1) the agreement between centralized pathology review and International Classification of Diseases for Oncology (ICD-0) codes assigned by pathologists at local institutions is low to moderate for uncommon histologies of breast cancer (e.g., mucinous and medulary); (2) risk factors for uncommon histologies are heterogeneous; (3) parity, age at menarch, and OC use are associated with mucinous; and (4) BMI and parity are associated with medullar.
we found that the risk factors for rare histologic subtypes (mucinous, medullay, tubular) of breast cancer differ from those for the most common histologic subtypes.

the identification of risk factors for uncommon histologies of breast cancer.
the risk factors for uncommon histological subtypes of breast cancers.
the epidemiology of less common histologic subtypes, and we demonstrate that centralized pathology review is necessary to study risk factors for these subtypes.

these results suggest that there is no association between breast cancer risk and the histologic types of tubular, medullary or mucinous carcinomas.
parity and BMI are associated with mucinous and medulalry breast cancer, respectively, but not tubular cancer.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of centralized review for histologic classification of breast cancers is important to accurately estimate the association of risk factors with uncommon tumor histologies.
the use of local pathology codes, as compared with centralized review, may result in biased estimates of risk factor associations for uncommon histologic types of invasive breast cancer.

we have shown that the risk factors associated with rare breast tumor histologies are different from those of common histologies and that the use of ICD-O coding for rare histologies is likely to result in biased relative risk estimates for risk factor studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are important differences in breast cancer risk factors across different histologic subtypes.
there are differences in the risk factors for different subtypes of breast cancers.

there is substantial heterogeneity in the risk factors associated with the various histologic subtypes, which suggests that the underlying etiology of breast cancers varies by histologic subtype, and that this heterogeneity is not adequately captured by ICD-O coding.
